title: Tenant-scoped TTL blueprints and signed evidence-bundle export workflow
creator: Anjali Rao
description: Deliver tenant-scoped TTL blueprints (declarative templates) for prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics plus a signed evidence-bundle export path. The goal is to let customers define compact, composable retention recipes that can be dry-run, simulated for cost/size impact, applied at route or tenant level, and exported as cryptographically signed evidence bundles for audits. This ticket covers product acceptance criteria, API surface, admin preview UI, and the end-to-end export format requirements for legal/infosec review.
acceptance_criteria: Customers can create TTL blueprints that target routes, models, and tags with inheritance and overrides
Admin UI shows a retention preview with estimated storage/cost and example sample of affected recent requests (dry-run)
Exported evidence bundle contains chain-of-custody manifest, per-request retention decision, PII score tags, and is signed with KMS-wrapped key
API supports scheduleable exports to S3/GCS/secure FTP and returns a signed manifest URL
Rollout plan includes a beta with opt-in tenants and migration playbook for existing retention rules
Security review sign-off and automated tests for evidence integrity and non-repudiation
notes: Motivation: customers in regulated industries need auditable proofs of data deletion and tamper-evident exports for legal discovery.
We will build on top of the TTL engine from ENG-19412 but introduce a blueprint/template layer for reusability across tenants.
Design should prioritise clear defaults: e.g., routes with high PII scores default to shorter TTLs unless explicitly overridden.
Signed evidence bundles must include a compact hash chain and KMS envelope metadata to support later verification by auditors.
Consider adding a 'legal-hold' flag that temporarily pauses deletions and appears in the export manifest.
Estimate assumes two backend engineers for 3 sprints + one frontend engineer for the admin preview UX.
design_feedback: Design reviewed 2025-02-20: smaller initial surface—support route-level and tenant-level blueprints, defer sampling policies to a follow-up (PM-47195)
UX requested an example-first experience in the admin preview: show 10 sample requests, explain why each would be retained/deleted
Privacy team: add explicit PII field provenance to the manifest (detector version and score)
engineering_updates: 2025-02-25: ENG spike complete. Two viable export formats identified: newline-delimited JSON bundle with separate signed manifest, or a single tar.gz with manifest.json and signed manifest.sig. Preferring tar.gz for transactional upload.
2025-03-01: DB migration plan drafted—add 'retention_decision_v2' column and soft-delete marker; will run backfill in controlled window.
2025-03-03: Prototype PR opened for export worker: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8241
Need: KMS integration checklist and service-account flow for cross-account S3 deliveries
open_risks: Large tenants with long retention windows could create very large evidence bundles—need server-side sampling policy or chunked exports
Legal-hold semantics conflicting with customer-initiated deletions require policy precedence rules
Cross-region data residency constraints: exports must honor destination region policies for tenant
next_steps: Finalize blueprint DSL by 2025-03-10 (PM + Privacy + Eng)
Ship admin preview mockups and get UX approval (Design review 2025-03-12)
Complete export worker MVP and end-to-end signed bundle upload to S3 test bucket (ENG target 2025-03-28)
Schedule security review and sign-off for KMS usage (security team 2025-03-20)
Prepare beta onboarding doc for customers including a migration playbook and sample manifests
